title: Backstage at Almost Television: how our AI-made puppet show gets made
author: Slackluster
selftext:
This is what we're working on: **Almost Television**, a weekly puppet sketch comedy show, and this is a short look backstage at how it's made, hosted by one of our puppets, Basil Quince.

How it works:

* **The studio is code.** The puppets, sets, props, cameras and lights are a 3D studio we built in Three.js. Every frame is rendered from it; no video generator draws anything.
* **AI writers' room.** Sketches are pitched by AI, other models read the scripts and give notes, and Claude helps write and direct each episode. A human showrunner picks what stays and gives notes on every cut.
* **Voices and music.** ElevenLabs does the voices, and an automated check listens to every take and redoes the ones that don't say their words. The house band's songs are made with Suno.
* **Weekly.** A new 11-to-13-minute episode every Saturday.

Everything in the video is true to how we work, just played for laughs.

The full episode it comes from: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wesrpFLIlAI](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wesrpFLIlAI)

Happy to answer anything about the pipeline!

comments.author: Guilty_Plate_6781
comments.body: If it's AI, I could use those cute puppet assets in a game idea.

replies.author: Slackluster
replies.body:
yeah, i mostly am a game developer with 25 years industry experience but this is my first attempt at non-interactive video entertainment.

i definitely want to make some games with these characters but right now focused on finishing season 1 with about 10 episodes, we are half way there!
